strings.name: Mikaela Shiffrin
strings.role: Skier · Alpine World Cup record setter
strings.summary: Shiffrin entered the Alpine World Cup as a teenager, mastering slalom before succeeding in giant slalom and speed events. She won Olympic slalom gold at eighteen, passed Ingemar Stenmark’s World Cup win record in 2023 and reached 100 victories in 2025. Injuries and comebacks punctuated her career. In 2026 she won another Olympic slalom gold and her sixth overall World Cup title.
strings.coverageNote: Sources checked through 13 November 2026. Selected career milestones; results and records refer to their cited dates, not an exhaustive results log or live ranking.
strings.influence.rationale: Set a new competitive benchmark for women's winter sports through record achievements in the Alpine Ski World Cup.
strings.facts.fact-1.label: Training
strings.facts.fact-1.value: Burke Mountain Academy; Ski & Snowboard Club Vail
strings.facts.fact-2.label: Events
strings.facts.fact-2.value: Slalom and giant slalom; also competes in speed events
strings.highlights.highlight-1.title: One hundred World Cup wins
strings.highlights.highlight-1.text: Won the Sestriere slalom in February 2025 to become the first Alpine skier with 100 World Cup victories.
strings.highlights.highlight-2.title: Three Olympic golds and six overall titles
strings.highlights.highlight-2.text: By March 2026, held three Olympic golds and six overall World Cup titles.
strings.timeline.event-1.title: Seventh in the Sölden opener
strings.timeline.event-1.text: Finished seventh in giant slalom at Sölden as she began a season emphasizing giant slalom and super-G.
strings.timeline.event-2.title: Sixth overall World Cup title
strings.timeline.event-2.text: Secured a sixth women’s overall title in Norway, equalling Annemarie Moser-Pröll’s record.
strings.timeline.event-3.title: Third Olympic gold
strings.timeline.event-3.text: Won slalom at Milano Cortina, adding to her 2014 slalom and 2018 giant slalom golds.
strings.timeline.event-4.title: One hundredth World Cup victory
strings.timeline.event-4.text: Won the Sestriere slalom after returning from an abdominal injury, reaching 100 World Cup wins.
strings.timeline.event-5.title: Passed Stenmark’s win record
strings.timeline.event-5.text: Won her 87th World Cup race in Åre, surpassing Ingemar Stenmark’s 86.
strings.timeline.event-6.title: Gold and silver in PyeongChang
strings.timeline.event-6.text: Won giant slalom gold and combined silver at the Winter Olympics.
strings.timeline.event-7.title: First overall World Cup title
strings.timeline.event-7.text: Won her first overall World Cup title, extending her success beyond slalom.
strings.timeline.event-8.title: Olympic slalom champion at eighteen
strings.timeline.event-8.text: Won slalom in Sochi at eighteen, becoming the youngest Olympic champion in the event.
strings.timeline.event-9.title: First world title
strings.timeline.event-9.text: Won the slalom world title in Schladming at seventeen at her first senior World Championships.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: First World Cup win
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Won the night slalom in Åre at seventeen for her first World Cup victory.
strings.timeline.event-11.title: World Cup debut
strings.timeline.event-11.text: Made her World Cup debut in giant slalom in Špindlerův Mlýn at fifteen.
strings.timeline.event-12.title: Born in the United States
strings.timeline.event-12.text: Grew up skiing in Colorado and later trained through Burke Mountain Academy and the Vail club system.
